title: Knowledge Boundary Probing and Demand-Guided Intervention for LLM-Based Power System Code Generation
problem: Open-weight LLMs for power-system code generation suffer from structured API-knowledge boundary errors, such as hallucinated function names and misused parameters, hindering reliable on-premise deployment.
key_idea: Introduces a boundary-aware intervention that combines query-side API demand estimation with targeted proactive documentation injection and routed reactive correction to address API-knowledge boundary errors.
method: Proposes PowerCodeBench benchmark, L0-L3 documentation-driven probing for per-model API knowledge profiles, and a demand-guided intervention that injects relevant documentation and applies reactive correction based on API demand estimation.
dataset_or_scenario: PowerCodeBench, a benchmark generator pairing natural-language operator queries with pandapower code and numerical ground truth; evaluated on 2,000 tasks.
metrics: Accuracy points (32 to 56 improvement), prompt-token cost (41% of baseline).
results_summary: The intervention improves every evaluated open-weight model of at least 7B parameters and every commercial API by 32 to 56 accuracy points, with open-weight models in 70B-120B range matching commercial mid-tier accuracy.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require further validation on other power system libraries or broader code generation tasks.

title: Ladder Logic Translation using Large Language Models in Industrial Automation
problem: Translating ladder logic programs between different PLC vendors (e.g., Rockwell to Siemens) is difficult due to mismatched environments, incompatible constructs, and black-box tools.
key_idea: A rigorous pipeline combining XML extraction, structural normalization, and a constrained LLM to automate ladder logic translation while preserving semantic consistency.
method: The pipeline includes XML extraction from Rockwell programs, structural normalization, a constrained generative function using an LLM, and integration via the TIA Portal Openness API for Siemens S7 output.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract; example case is Rockwell to Siemens PLC code translation.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract; results mention high semantic consistency across instruction categories.
results_summary: The translations retain high semantic consistency across instruction categories, indicating effective automated translation.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on specific vendor formats and constrained LLM generalizability.

title: Mellum2 Technical Report
problem: Developing an efficient, open-weight language model specialized for software engineering tasks that balances performance with inference efficiency on commodity GPUs.
key_idea: A 12B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with only 2.5B active parameters per token, incorporating a Multi-Token Prediction head for speculative decoding and a three-phase curriculum pre-training.
method: Uses a MoE architecture (64 experts, 8 active) with Grouped-Query Attention, Sliding Window Attention, and a Multi-Token Prediction head. Pre-trained on 10.6T tokens with a three-phase curriculum, optimized with Muon under FP8 precision, then extended to 128K context via YaRN and post-trained with SFT and RLVR.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Competitive with open-weight baselines in the 4B-14B range across code generation, math, reasoning, tool use, knowledge, and safety benchmarks while running at the compute of a 2.5B dense model.

title: Fighting Numerical Hallucinations via Data-centric Compilation for Online Financial QA
problem: Large Language Models suffer from numerical reasoning hallucinations in financial question answering, and existing model-centric approaches fail to address noise sensitivity, calculation fragility, and auditability crisis in an integrated manner.
key_idea: A data-centric paradigm that synthesizes adversarial training data and uses a compile-and-execute inference process to ensure faithful numerical reasoning by design.
method: The Data-centric Reasoning Compiler (DCRC) framework with three phases: adversarial data construction, multi-stage training to produce a Data-centric Structuring Agent (DSA), and compile-and-execute inference where DSA transforms queries and documents into verifiable executable programs.
dataset_or_scenario: Established offline benchmarks and a real-world online financial QA system.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Not specified in the abstract

title: Incremental BPE Tokenization
problem: Standard BPE tokenization processes the entire input text at once, which is inefficient for streaming settings and can cause latency in large language model pipelines.
key_idea: The paper proposes an incremental BPE tokenization algorithm that processes each input byte in O(log^2 t) time, enabling efficient partial tokenization and streaming output.
method: The algorithm incrementally maintains BPE tokenization results for every prefix of the input text by implementing the standard BPE merge procedure with a fixed set of merge rules, and introduces an eager output algorithm for streaming.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Speedup factor and latency reductions compared to Hugging Face's tokenizers and OpenAI's tiktoken.
results_summary: The approach achieves up to ~3x speedup over Hugging Face's tokenizers and significant latency reductions over OpenAI's tiktoken on pathological inputs.

title: ExpGraph: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory for LLM Agents
problem: LLM agents often solve tasks from scratch and fail to reuse successful strategies or failure lessons from prior experience, and fine-tuning is inflexible when stronger executors emerge.
key_idea: A model-agnostic experience learning framework that enables frozen and replaceable LLM executors to improve through external experience reuse without parameter updates, using a self-evolving experience graph.
method: ExpGraph summarizes historical trajectories into reusable skills and failure lessons, organizes them as nodes in a self-evolving experience graph, retrieves experiences via graph diffusion and utility-aware ranking, and trains a lightweight retrieval copilot with reinforcement learning using executor performance feedback.
dataset_or_scenario: ExpSuite covering question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and multi-step agentic environments including ALFWorld and AppWorld.
metrics: Improvement over baseline (percentage), average interaction steps reduction.
results_summary: ExpGraph improves over the strongest baseline by 12.2% and 4.7% on static tasks with smaller and larger executors, and by 21.4% and 12.7% in agentic environments, while reducing average interaction steps by 12.7% and 21.6%.

title: Healthcare Mechanisms from Policy-as-Code Search under Strategic Provider Response
problem: Existing healthcare AI benchmarks hold provider response fixed and cannot evaluate mechanisms by the equilibrium they produce, failing to account for strategic behavior.
key_idea: Recasting hospital mechanism design as program synthesis for language models, using typed, inspectable rule programs executed in a multi-agent simulator with strategic provider channels.
method: An incentive sweep recovers classical health-economics findings, and LLM-guided evolutionary code search over rule-program space synthesizes an inspectable mixed-objective program.
dataset_or_scenario: Medi-Sim, a multi-agent simulator with five strategic provider channels (coding, selection, delay, effort, triage).
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (e.g., elimination of up-coding, halving rejection, retaining funds).
results_summary: The synthesized program eliminates up-coding, halves rejection, and retains most of the profit-oriented baseline's funds, while an audit lever exposes pressure migration.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may depend on simulator fidelity and generalizability to real-world settings.

title: Improving Small Language Models for Code Generation with Reinforcement Learning from Verification Feedback
problem: How to effectively use reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) to improve code generation in small language models, and how reward design impacts functional correctness and behavioral properties.
key_idea: Empirical study of RLVR for Python code generation using small models, comparing different reward formulations (unit-test, static-analysis, combined) and group-based policy optimization variants (GRPO, GSPO).
method: Applied RLVR with LoRA fine-tuning on Qwen3-0.6B and Llama3.2-1B models, using GRPO and GSPO with unit-test-only, static-analysis-only (Ruff linter), and combined rewards.
dataset_or_scenario: MBPP benchmark for Python code generation.
metrics: pass@1, generation length, Ruff severity profiles, execution error types.
results_summary: RLVR improved pass@1 by up to 13 percentage points with combined reward; static-analysis-only rewards biased toward shorter completions without improving correctness, while combined rewards yielded better trade-offs.
limitations: Study limited to small models (0.6B and 1B parameters) and a single benchmark (MBPP); findings may not generalize to larger models or other datasets.

title: SEAL: Can Saturated Benchmarks Be Revived by LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge?
problem: Standard benchmarks for language models are saturated, with near-tied scores that fail to distinguish model performance, and constructing harder benchmarks is costly.
key_idea: Existing saturated benchmarks can be made informative again by using an improved evaluation protocol (LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge) that extracts latent ranking signals from the same candidate outputs.
method: SEAL (Seeded Elimination with Adaptive LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge) is a self-improving evaluation protocol that seeds candidate outputs into a single-elimination tournament, evaluating each match with task-level principles and self-improving checklist criteria.
dataset_or_scenario: Multiple saturated benchmarks covering code generation, mathematical reasoning, knowledge-intensive question answering, and tool-use agent task completion.
metrics: Spearman rank correlation, top-1 agreement, number of LLM calls per task.
results_summary: SEAL achieves 0.83–1.00 Spearman agreement with full pairwise judging and 4/4 top-1 agreement, while requiring only 11.89 calls per task compared to 28.00 for full pairwise evaluation.

title: Convergence Theory for Iterative LLM-Based Neural Architecture Search: A Parametric Cross-Entropy Framework with Closed-Form Proxy Reliability
problem: No formal convergence theory exists for iterative LLM-based neural architecture search (NAS) algorithms.
key_idea: Modeling iterative LLM-NAS as a parametric Cross-Entropy method over executable programs and proving convergence properties, including a closed-form expression for proxy reliability.
method: Formalizes iterative LLM fine-tuning on elite architectures as a CE update, proves monotonic improvement and geometric convergence, introduces delta-based generation and MinHash-Jaccard novelty filter, and derives a closed-form proxy reliability formula.
dataset_or_scenario: 22-cycle, three-LLM, six-dataset experiment with 3,300 generated architectures.
metrics: Expected architecture quality, valid-generation rate, proxy reliability (rho_S).
results_summary: Confirmed two predictions quantitatively and two at direction-of-effect level; explained the previously unreported proxy-reliability ceiling effect.

title: Learning to Choose: An Empowerment-Guided Multi-Agent System with semantic communication for Adaptive Method Selection
problem: Automating scientific computing workflows requires autonomous systems to select appropriate computational strategies and ensure causal attribution, but multi-agent pipelines suffer from semantic drift where executed procedures diverge from original strategies, corrupting evaluation and adaptation.
key_idea: Introduces a multi-agent framework combining contextual bandits with structured inter-agent communication and semantic checkpoints to preserve action-outcome fidelity, interpreted through the lens of empowerment.
method: The system integrates specialized LLM agents, grounded code generation, and self-healing execution loops within an adaptive decision-making architecture, using contextual bandits for method selection and semantic checkpoints to ensure consistency across agents.
dataset_or_scenario: Sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification workflows as representative case studies.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (mentions convergence, robustness, and adaptation qualitatively).
results_summary: Unchecked semantic drift degrades policy learning, while the proposed framework improves convergence, robustness, and adaptation to novel problem contexts.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require further validation on broader scientific workflows.

title: CodeGolf Bench: A Multi-Language Benchmark for Evaluating Concise Code Generation Capabilities of Large Language Models
problem: Existing benchmarks for evaluating LLM code generation are limited by fixed problem sets and language coverage, and do not measure the ability to produce concise, efficient code.
key_idea: Introduces a benchmark based on code golf, a competition focused on minimal character solutions, to evaluate LLMs' concise code generation across 60 programming languages with dynamic problems and live human baselines.
method: Leverages the code.golf platform to provide new problems and live human performance baselines; evaluates nine LLMs on Python and C++ tasks, comparing reasoning and non-reasoning models.
dataset_or_scenario: CodeGolf Bench benchmark covering 60 programming languages, with evaluation on Python and C++ tasks from the code.golf platform.
metrics: Average percentile performance relative to human baselines.
results_summary: Reasoning models significantly outperform non-reasoning models, achieving best average percentile of 70.97%, with the gap more pronounced in C++ due to strict syntax requirements.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on code.golf platform availability and focus on character count rather than other efficiency metrics.

title: Inferring Code Correctness from Specification
problem: Validating the correctness of LLM-generated code remains a critical challenge; existing approaches are either costly due to dynamic consensus or susceptible to bugs and bias in static reasoning.
key_idea: Grounding LLM reasoning with concrete (input, output) pairs derived from the specification, avoiding reasoning over the code itself.
method: TRAILS generates diverse test inputs via category partitioning based on the specification, executes them against candidate code, and prompts LLMs to assess whether input-output pairs conform to the specification, aggregating scores across inputs.
dataset_or_scenario: LiveCodeBench and CoCoClaNeL datasets, evaluated across three LLMs (Qwen3Coder-30B, Devstral-Small-24B, Olmo3.1-Instruct).
metrics: Matthew Correlation Coefficient (MCC), stability across seeded runs, and number of unique code samples correctly labeled.
results_summary: TRAILS improves MCC by up to 39% relative to Zero-Shot CoT, consistently outperforms HoarePrompt, and demonstrates greater stability and coverage.

title: Minimal Prompt Perturbations Lead to Code Vulnerabilities: Prompt Fragility and Hidden-State Signals in Coding LLMs
problem: Whether minor prompt perturbations compromise the security of LLM-generated code, beyond functional correctness.
key_idea: Token-level mutations as small as a single-character change can flip generated code from secure to vulnerable, and this fragility is partially encoded in hidden states.
method: Applied token-level mutations to prompts across three models and five programming languages, then probed hidden states to predict vulnerabilities.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Mean AUC for predicting input-handling vulnerabilities (0.753) and secure-defaults vulnerabilities (0.674).
results_summary: Single-character prompt mutations can flip code from secure to vulnerable; input-handling vulnerabilities are more predictable from hidden states than secure-defaults vulnerabilities.

title: HTAM: Hierarchical Transition-Attended Memory for Operator Optimization
problem: LLM-based GPU operator optimization faces a granularity mismatch: coarse hints are reusable but hard to execute, while detailed memories are actionable but enlarge the search space and obscure optimization bottlenecks.
key_idea: Proposes a coarse-to-fine framework that organizes optimization experience into a hierarchical transition graph (HTG) with global directions, local strategies, and transition experience.
method: HTAM builds a two-level HTG to organize coarse global directions, detailed local strategies, and transition experience. At each evolution step, it selects a global direction based on current state and history, retrieves corresponding local strategy memory, and uses it to guide CUDA code generation.
dataset_or_scenario: Full KernelBench suite, backend and Robust-KBench studies
metrics: Correctness, fast-solution rate, speedup
results_summary: HTAM consistently improves correctness, fast-solution rate, and speedup over LLM-based baselines, with transferable benefits from structured memory shown in backend and Robust-KBench studies.

title: NaRA: Noise-Aware LoRA for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Diffusion LLMs
problem: Existing PEFT methods like LoRA are designed for autoregressive models and ignore the dynamics of the diffusion process, where input distributions and generation difficulty vary with noise level, leading to suboptimal fine-tuning of diffusion LLMs.
key_idea: Introduce a noise-aware low-rank adaptation (NaRA) that uses a lightweight hypernetwork to generate low-rank core matrices conditioned on noise level, enabling update matrices to vary continuously along the denoising trajectory.
method: NaRA adds a low-rank core matrix generated by a globally shared hypernetwork conditioned on noise level, allowing dynamic updates while keeping parameter and latency overhead negligible.
dataset_or_scenario: Commonsense reasoning, mathematical reasoning, and code generation benchmarks.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (likely accuracy or pass@k based on benchmarks).
results_summary: NaRA consistently outperforms noise-agnostic baselines across commonsense reasoning, mathematical reasoning, and code generation benchmarks.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require tuning of hypernetwork architecture or noise conditioning.

title: Reliable Reasoning with Large Language Models via Preference-Based Maximum Satisfiability
problem: LLMs struggle with optimisation tasks involving multiple constraints and user-defined preferences, which are common in domains like robotics.
key_idea: Externalize reasoning through code generation: LLMs generate Python code encoding constraints and preferences as a preference-based MaxSAT problem, solved by an exact solver, with independent verification.
method: LLMs generate Python code that encodes user-defined constraints and preferences as a preference-based MaxSAT problem, solved by an exact MaxSAT solver; solutions are verified for feasibility and optimality against a canonical encoding.
dataset_or_scenario: Three families of preference-based reasoning tasks.
metrics: Acceptance rates (feasibility and optimality).
results_summary: The MaxSAT-based pipeline achieves substantially higher acceptance rates than baselines (direct-answer, chain-of-thought, program-of-thought), in some cases exceeding 80%.

title: Cluster-Level Attention-Guided Parallel Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models
problem: Existing training-free samplers for masked diffusion language models decide which positions to commit at token-level granularity, which may be suboptimal for parallel decoding efficiency.
key_idea: Reliable predictions often emerge as contiguous high-confidence spans, so the unit of parallel commitment can be larger than a single token; self-attention maps can estimate inter-cluster dependencies for conflict-aware selection.
method: Group adjacent high-confidence tokens into confidence-induced clusters (CICs) as span-level update units, then use self-attention maps to select mutually compatible CICs for parallel commitment, forming a training-free cluster-level decoder (CLAD).
dataset_or_scenario: Four reasoning and code-generation benchmarks, evaluated on LLaDA and Dream model families.
metrics: Speedup (1.77x--8.47x) and task accuracy (broadly comparable).
results_summary: CLAD achieves 1.77x--8.47x speedups over Vanilla decoding while maintaining broadly comparable task accuracy in most settings.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations may include reliance on confidence thresholds and applicability to diverse tasks.

title: On the Road to Personalized Code Intelligence: Portraiting and Assisting Developers Based on Their In-IDE Behaviors
problem: Current one-size-fits-all code intelligence systems fail to accommodate individual developer differences in tool-chain preferences, domain expertise, and problem-solving strategies.
key_idea: Introduces VirtualME, an IDE-embedded data infrastructure that continuously captures and interprets dynamic developer behaviors to build a personalized developer persona.
method: VirtualME has three components: log-level behavior extraction, task-level behavior recognition via a multi-agent pipeline, and developer-personality measurement using a rule engine to distill a four-dimensional persona. It integrates this persona into a personalized repository-level knowledge Q&A agent.
dataset_or_scenario: A multi-repository benchmark with real-world developer trajectories.
metrics: Five dimensions of answer quality (not specified in detail), with average 33.80% improvement over generic baselines.
results_summary: VirtualME-enhanced answers outperform generic baselines on five dimensions, yielding an average 33.80% improvement, demonstrating the value of continuous developer-behavior data for personalized code intelligence.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on IDE-specific data and the complexity of multi-agent pipeline.

title: SafeRx-Agent: A Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Safe and Explainable Medication Recommendation
problem: Existing medication recommendation methods either predict structured drug codes with limited evidence grounding or lack safety verification and traceability, while current benchmarks ignore subgroup-level safety differences.
key_idea: Introduces a fine-grained medication recommendation setting based on fourth-level ATC code generation and a multi-agent framework that integrates patient context, external clinical knowledge, and safety verification.
method: SafeRx-Agent is a knowledge-grounded multi-agent framework that uses patient context, external clinical knowledge, and safety verification to recommend traceable medication sets.
dataset_or_scenario: MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV datasets
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: SafeRx-Agent improves fine-grained medication prediction accuracy while controlling drug interactions, contraindications, and medication set size.
